resources.string: Apps that embed the Grom engine register here and heartbeat every 30 seconds.
Managed by the host app; Grom does not start or stop it.
Grom turns this phone into a small server. Apps that include it get their own place to store data and their own API routes \u2014 on the phone itself, with no account and no cloud.
Most people need no rented server

If an app only has to work while the phone is with you, everything stays on the phone. Nothing to rent, nothing to configure, no monthly cost. The phone has to stay switched on and the app has to stay installed.

Some systems must run all the time, even while the phone is locked or charging. For those you can connect your own server: type its address, user name and a password or key, and the phone opens the tunnel itself. Grom forwards only its API port \u2014 never a shell, never your files. Extra servers are optional and always under your control.

Grom can hold your public Nostr key and a list of relays so your other software can read them from one place. It does not open relay connections itself: adding a relay is only a note to yourself. For Lightning you either point Grom at your own backend or keep a reference to a node that runs elsewhere; the probe in the menu is the only thing that checks it, and until it has run the answer is honestly \u201cnot probed\u201d.

Every app that includes Grom says hello here and keeps saying it while it runs. The lamp is green while that app is alive and grey when it has not checked in for a while. Each app only sees its own storage. Removing an entry does not stop the app: a running app announces itself again within about half a minute.

If the phone is off, has no network, or Android stops the app, nothing is served and no alert is sent \u2014 nothing else is watching. A red lamp means a measured failure; a grey one means nothing has been checked yet. There is no uptime promise and no silent retry that pretends to work.
Grom never invents a connection: if the link is down, the lamp is red and the screen says so.
A reference only. Grom stores where your node lives and never connects to it: LND, Core Lightning and NWC stay on your own server.

If you want to hear about a crash, a stopped server or a broken link without staring at the screen, switch on Telegram alerts: create a bot, paste its token and your chat id, and the phone sends you a short message when something changes. The message is one fixed sentence \u2014 never a password, an address or an amount. If the phone is off or the app was closed, nothing is sent, because the phone is the one sending.

Why Android may be stopping the server
Your phone measures, you decide. Grom changes nothing here: it reports what Android answered and opens the settings page you need. A grey row means this phone did not answer — not that it is fine.
The server is not running, so Grom reports only what this phone can tell without it.
What Grom cannot see from here

Android does not let an app read the Doze whitelist, the phantom-process limit or a vendor\'s auto-start list. Those are the questions only your computer can answer, so Grom shows you the commands and you run them. It never runs them for you.
